name: UX Patterns & Persuasive Best Practices
description: The tactical toolkit of evidence-based UX patterns that influence how users perceive, evaluate, and act. Organized around four behavioral objectives: getting attention, creating a positive impression, winning conscious evaluation, and making action easy. Each pattern is grounded in cognitive psychology and behavioral economics research.

subskills.name: Get Attention — Salience & Noticeability
subskills.description: Design patterns that ensure the right element is noticed at the right moment. Covers visual salience (contrast, motion, size), notification design (push, email, in-app), empty state design that draws the eye, and F/Z-pattern layout optimization. Applies the Von Restorff Effect (the isolated item is remembered) and Attentional Spotlight theory.

subskills.name: Create Positive First Impression
subskills.description: Patterns that establish trust, delight, and credibility on first encounter. Covers aesthetic-usability effect (beautiful designs are perceived as easier to use), brand consistency, typography and color psychology, micro-animations that signal quality, loading skeleton screens that reduce perceived wait time, and first-run experience design.

subskills.name: Win Evaluation — Social Proof
subskills.description: Cialdini's social proof principle: people look to others' behavior when uncertain about what to do. Implementations: user review counts and ratings, testimonials, 'X people are viewing this' indicators, user-generated content, case studies, and social media follower counts. Distinguishes between quantitative social proof (counts) and qualitative (reviews, testimonials).

subskills.name: Win Evaluation — Authority
subskills.description: Establishing credibility through demonstrated expertise and trusted endorsements. Covers expert recommendations, celebrity endorsements, certifications and badges (SSL, ISO, awards), media mentions ('as seen in...'), verified badges, professional credentials displayed in UI, and trust seals on checkout flows.

subskills.name: Win Evaluation — Loss Aversion
subskills.description: Kahneman & Tversky's Prospect Theory: losses loom larger than equivalent gains (loss aversion ratio ~2:1). UX applications: free trial expiry warnings, 'don't lose your progress' nudges, countdown timers for expiring offers, limited seat warnings, and framing copy as avoiding a loss rather than achieving a gain.

subskills.name: Win Evaluation — Peer Comparison
subskills.description: Showing users how they compare to relevant peers to motivate behavior change. Covers personalized benchmarks ('You're in the top 20% of users'), anonymized peer comparisons, cohort-based progress reports, leaderboards with opt-in privacy controls, and normative messaging ('Most users complete this in 5 minutes').

subskills.name: Make Action Easy — Urgency & Scarcity
subskills.description: Time and quantity constraints that trigger immediate action. Covers real urgency (genuine deadlines, actual stock limits) vs manufactured urgency (ethical considerations), countdown timers, low-stock indicators, limited-time offer badges, and flash sale design. Includes ethical guidelines on avoiding dark patterns (fake scarcity).

subskills.name: Make Action Easy — Implementation Intentions
subskills.description: Gollwitzer's implementation intention research: if-then planning dramatically increases follow-through on intended behaviors. UX applications include prompted scheduling ('When do you want to do this?'), calendar integration, pre-commitment flows, and reminder personalization that anchors the action to a specific time and context.

subskills.name: Make Action Easy — Friction Reduction & Defaulting
subskills.description: Minimizing the effort required to take the target action. Covers one-click flows, pre-filled forms, smart defaults, reducing steps in checkout/signup funnels, progressive form disclosure, autofill, and re-engagement flows that pick up where the user left off. Applies Fogg's Ability dimension to maximize the chance that motivation × ability × prompt converges successfully.
